column1: # Onygenales + Eurotiales (Eurotiomycetes) adhesion / surface-protein candidate seeds.
# DRAFT, literature survey 2026-09-27. Built to close the coverage gap recorded in
# docs/model-review/STATUS.md: A. fumigatus had 7 labeled proteins of 895 surface proteins,
# PROVENANCE: PubMed (searched 2026-09-27) + UniProtKB REST. Every row traces to a PMID or a
# database record. Accessions were resolved by query, not guessed; where a protein could not
# be resolved the uniprot_query is blank and evidence_summary says so.
#   adhesins        E1 direct experimental adhesion/binding evidence (deletion or binding assay)
#                   E2 family membership, or weaker (phenotype only, antibody blocking, no deletion)
#   hard negatives  N1 characterized non-adhesive function
#                   N2 adhesin-like architecture, no adhesion evidence
# NOTE ON MOONLIGHTING: several Onygenales "adhesins" are cytoplasmic proteins found on the
# cell surface (Hsp60, enolase). They mediate host binding but are NOT secreted-pathway
# surface proteins and will not be in a signal-peptide-defined stage-1 population. They are
# marked moonlighting=yes and should be held OUT of stage-2 training, not used as positives.

column10: evidence_summary

Spherule outer wall glycoprotein; rSOWgp binds laminin>fibronectin>collagen IV; targeted deletion reduces ECM binding and virulence; 4-6 copies of a 41-47 aa Pro/Asp-rich repeat, size varies by isolate
Larger SOWgp allele (375 aa, 5 repeats); same family as Q8NK60, isolate-level repeat-number variation
422 aa allele with 6 tandem repeats; family member of the E1 adhesin
Proline-rich GPI-anchored cell-surface antigen, major vaccine/diagnostic antigen; adhesion NOT directly demonstrated - listed as surface protein candidate, needs binding assay
Surface adhesin and virulence factor; binds macrophage CR3 and CD14; knockout attenuated; also released in soluble form and suppresses TNF-alpha

Surface-localized Hsp60 is the ligand for macrophage CD11b/CD18 (CR3); rHsp60 blocks yeast attachment. Mitochondrial chaperonin moonlighting on the surface - no signal peptide, so out of scope for a secretion-defined stage 1

Yeast-phase-specific cell wall protein, also released; binds chitin and re-associates with the cell surface. UNRESOLVED in UniProt - searches on gene YPS3 and taxonomy 5037 returned nothing; add the locus tag when known
Secreted calcium-binding virulence factor, not an adhesin; a secreted-protein negative for Onygenales

Binds laminin and fibronectin; anti-gp43 blocks adhesion to Vero cells. Annotated as a glucan 1,3-beta-glucosidase, so enzyme-and-adhesin - a useful test of the enzyme-implies-non-adhesin rule used in surface.tsv
Endochitinase 1 / complement-fixation antigen; immunodominant diagnostic antigen but an enzyme, not an adhesin. Good hard negative: highly antigenic AND non-adhesive

Surface CalA binds host integrin alpha5beta1 and mediates epithelial/endothelial invasion; deletion attenuates virulence; anti-CalA antibody protects mice. 177 aa, no GPI - the architecture the current model cannot see
Repeat-rich GPI-anchored CWP; deletion reduces conidial adhesion, but the primary phenotype is cell-wall integrity. Repeat number varies between isolates and is used for strain typing

RodA forms the conidial rodlet layer; mediates attachment to hydrophobic surfaces and masks conidia from immune recognition. Attachment is a surface-property effect, not receptor-ligand binding - class differs from GPI adhesins
Second class I hydrophobin; no independent adhesion evidence found

Abundant secreted cell-wall mannoprotein and virulence factor, but the mechanism is sequestration of arachidonic acid via a hydrophobic LBD2 cavity - immune evasion, NOT adhesion. Strong hard negative: abundant surface mannoprotein with a demonstrated non-adhesive mechanism

GPI-anchored CFEM hemophore; the CfmA-C triple deletion affects cell-wall stability but NOT virulence, biofilm or heme uptake. CFEM is the clade-spanning family, so an experimentally non-adhesive CFEM member is a valuable negative
As cfmA; triple-deletion phenotype limited to cell-wall stability
GPI-anchored beta-1,3-glucanosyltransferase; cell-wall biosynthetic enzyme. Onygenales/Eurotiales counterpart of the S. cerevisiae Gas1 negative
GPI cell-wall protein; deletion affects conidial cell-wall integrity. Interacts genetically with cspA but is itself a structural/integrity protein
Conidial pigment biosynthesis laccase. AA1 is the family the shipped model over-calls kingdom-wide, so an explicit Eurotiales AA1 negative is important

Major allergen and secreted surface-associated protein; binds plasminogen/complement regulators in some reports but is not an established adhesin. Flagged for review, also relevant to the planned allergen category (#19)
